claim: For a continuous-time birth–death population with \(N=3\), unit birth rates, and two environments whose death-to-birth ratios are \( (x,y)\) and \( (y,x)\) at mutant counts \(1,2\), let switching be composition-dependent: \( +\to- \) occurs at rate \(e\) at count \(1\) and \(M\) at count \(2\), with reverse rates \(M\) and \(e\). For \(0<x<y\) and \(e,M>0\), fixation from one mutant in environment \(+\) exceeds both fixed-environment probabilities if and only if \(xM^2+(xy-e)M-e(e+1)(y+1)>0\), equivalently \(M>M_*\) for the positive root \(M_*=[e-xy+\sqrt{(xy-e)^2+4xe(e+1)(y+1)}]/(2x)\). With only \(N=2\) individuals and one transient mutant-count state, switching cannot exceed the best fixed-environment fixation probability. For \(x=2,y=3,e=1/10,M=10\), the switching model gives \(181/1373\), above the fixed-environment values \(1/9\) and \(1/10\).

scientific_limitations_and_integrity.novelty_limit: The inspected closest literature assumes exogenous environmental switching; broader literature on population-dependent switching remains a residual risk.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.proved: Exact fixation threshold for the specified \(N=3\) rate family; impossibility of exceeding the best frozen environment for \(N=2\) with one transient count and unit birth rates.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.reproducibility: An embedded standard-library script checks the representative case with exact rational arithmetic; the symbolic threshold is proved in RESULT.md.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.unproved: No general classification for arbitrary rate matrices, larger populations, more environments, or empirically calibrated switching mechanisms.

title: A sharp minimal-population threshold for feedback-enabled fixation
